Crucible is very much a mixed bag, as one can easily see indicated by its current review score average. I recently did a full-length game review video on the topic, (it's linked down below!) but here are just a few pro/con observations:

Pros:
-Each hero has their own unique playstyle and toolset, No two heroes feel even remotely identical.
-The maps are pretty decent, with lots of flanking routes, chokepoints, and areas of interest.
-The game doesn't have lootboxes! (Yet....)

Cons:
-The game is very poorly optimized. Lots of notable frame drops and framerate issues, even with Vsync on.
-The modes all feel somewhat identical. 
-The cosmetic store in-game has truly lazy-looking skins.
-Why this game has 3 paid premium editions is beyond explanation.

This game is halfway to a decent game, but really feels like it is early in development. Weapons don't feel like they have weight, and it is hard to gauge effectiveness in combat or to even know your weapons are hitting. While the game is attractive, there is a disconnect between you the player and the game elements as movement feels slow and clunky, and needed information isn't immersive or presented to the player in a logical manner. 

At no point in play did I feel engaged with this game, or have that rush I get with other competitive games.

Unfortunately, in this competitive market of team based first or third person shooters such as Fortnite, Apex Legends, Overwatch, etc., Crucible is way behind the curve. There are some creative elements, and decent graphics, but game play should be the primary focus, and it feels like it was the last consideration.

It is free to play, so try it out for yourselves, but I can't recommend this game currently.

There's no in game communication (from what I've seen) and the pinging system when you compare it to fortnite or apex is a level down. The skill explanations should be easier to find and the explanations should be more consistent wherever you find it. The tutorial is okay and teaches the CORE BASICS but a lot of my knowledge of the in-depth game comes from videos (which isnt a bad thing) and I believe they should teach more in the tutorial from beginning to end. However, I still feel the game has a lot of potential and it's better to hope for success of a game rather than hope for its failure.
